claim.summary: In the recorded proper charged F4 quotient, for degF<=a and a+|T|<=D, R_D(F L_T,label) has support a union of complete coordinate-subgroup orbits in G=F3^E/cutspace. A nonzero image therefore forces the image of F3^T into any subgroup making it homogeneous. For a finite family of weighted conjunction errors, with E_live the union of supports of nonzero errors, every common grading subgroup contains the coordinate image of E_live and has codimension at most |E minus E_live|-n+c(G minus E_live), counting isolated vertices. No extra +1 buffer, matching condition, disjointness or sparse weight is needed. This is an extracted corollary of the earlier proportional-column orbit proof, not a new mechanism; general mixtures can cancel surviving conjunction pieces.
claim.assessment: Working explicit corollary, medium reviewed after a MathJax correction. Full old orbit proof implies whole-orbit survival after arbitrary linear combinations. The degree-one weighted opening matches the bound after adding the weight's support direction. No numerical rerun or new within-sector contraction is supplied.
